subject.title: [Bug]: Slack provider doesn't reliably reload after channels.slack.botToken rotation (cached singleAuthorization)

question: Should maintainers require a current-main or newest-release Sandpaw/container reproduction before queueing any fix for this Slack token reload report?
rationale: Source inspection and a contributor run support the normal direct-edit path, but the reported miss could be watcher health, container filesystem behavior, or Control UI/config.patch scheduling; automation cannot safely choose the repair layer without that proof.

options.title: Require boundary reproduction
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask for the container/control-plane evidence listed in the latest maintainer comment before any fix PR is queued.

options.title: Harden watcher first
options.body: Proceed with generic watcher/container hardening even though the Control UI/config.patch path may be the real missed boundary.

options.title: Force Control UI restart follow-up
options.body: Add an explicit Control UI/config.patch channel restart follow-up, accepting possible duplicate behavior if the watcher path is actually healthy.

recommendation.title: Require boundary reproduction
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask for the container/control-plane evidence listed in the latest maintainer comment before any fix PR is queued.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the live assignee and has the strongest history across reload planning, in-memory config write reloads, and Slack plugin reload metadata.
